clue.text: The favourite's certain to win a little bit

blocks.note: a snip is a dead cert, something sure to succeed
a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A tipster says the favourite is sure to win, and recommends a small flutter.
explanation.walkthrough: The favourite's piece comes after the certainty piece. A snip, in British slang, is a bargain or a sure thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A snippet is a small piece or fragment cut from something larger, such as a scrap of news.

clue.text: Almost 108 gallons of sherry in old brass

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the measure is dropped

blocks.note: sack is an old name for a dry white wine such as sherry
a butt is a large cask, traditionally holding 108 gallons

explanation.surface: A huge cask of sherry is stored in an antique brass vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' joins the cask to its contents, which come first in the answer; 'old brass' is not metal but an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The sackbut is the Renaissance ancestor of the trombone, an early instrument of the brass family.

clue.text: Shocked query about new cars is unhinged

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so these letters are put together in a fresh order
about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: taken as written
unhinged read literally is not hinged
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone appalled by the latest models of car exclaims that the world has gone mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unhinged' read literally means not hinged, and the cars, shuffled, are parked inside the word for hinged.
explanation.definitionFit: Is nothing sacred? is the exclamation of someone outraged that cherished things are being disrespected.

clue.text: He claimed the place of the steam locomotive

definitions.text: the place of the steam locomotive

blocks.note: first meaning: one who lays claim to a throne

blocks.clueFragment: the place of the steam locomotive
blocks.note: second meaning, split in two: the engine runs in front of its coal wagon, the tender

explanation.surface: Someone boasted of having once stood where the old steam engine stood.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second meaning as PRE-TENDER: a steam locomotive is coupled ahead of its tender, the wagon carrying coal and water.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretender is a claimant, especially one asserting a right to a throne held by someone else.

clue.text: Chief island's headgear

blocks.note: top means chief or foremost
I is the abbreviation for island, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: The headdress worn by the leading man of an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Topis are pith helmets, lightweight sun hats worn in the tropics, so they count as headgear.

clue.text: Rue bolt being off gun? I can fix it

indicators.note: being off means gone wrong or out of place, so these letters must be put right in another order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a shooter is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: Someone regrets that a bolt has come off a gun, and a handyman offers to mend it.
explanation.definitionFit: A troubleshooter is a person called in to diagnose and solve problems, who might well say these words.

clue.text: Short pants shortened at either end available in Northants.

indicators.note: shortened means one letter is lost, and with the same letter at each end it does not matter which end goes
available suggests the letters are free to be used in any order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A shop advertises abbreviated shorts on sale in a Northamptonshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop one S from SHORTPANTS and rearrange the rest. Thrapston is a small market town in Northamptonshire, an English county abbreviated Northants.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrapston is a market town located within the county of Northamptonshire in the English Midlands.

clue.text: He has now upset the Queen

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters fall into another order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A man has just offended the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: An owner is a person who has or possesses something, so the phrase describes him exactly.

clue.text: 10 (logarithm of 1 some calculate) in obstruction of factor in jet lag

indicators.note: some means only part of the following word is used, its opening stretch with the tail cut off
in places the bracketed material inside the word for an obstruction

blocks.note: the number ten written with the digits read as letters, I and O
log is the usual abbreviation for logarithm
the digit one looks like the letter I
taken as written, then cut down to its first four letters
a block is an obstruction

explanation.surface: A mock-mathematical formula in brackets claims to describe what causes jet lag.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed sum looks like real maths, but each item just supplies letters, and the whole lot sits inside the obstruction after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The body's internal clock governs sleep cycles, and its disruption by crossing time zones is what causes jet lag.

clue.text: Greek character piles on the agony

indicators.note: something in agony writhes and twists, so these letters are contorted into another order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A melodramatic Greek figure exaggerates their suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piles on the agony' is a set phrase for exaggerating, which disguises where the fodder ends and the signal begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsilon is the fifth letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a character.

clue.text: Most European characters need Tory leadership to come alive with

indicators.note: characters means letters, here taken as loose letters to be set out afresh

blocks.note: Con is short for Conservative, a Tory; leadership puts it at the front
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Euro politics: most of Europe's leaders must have a Conservative at their head to come to life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most European' looks like a superlative, but both words are the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Things contemporaneous with each other exist at the same period, so one is alive at the same time as the other.

clue.text: Night flier, male, to take to the water

blocks.note: a bat flies by night
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A nocturnal male creature takes a dip.
explanation.definitionFit: To bathe is to swim or go into the sea or a river for pleasure.

clue.text: Magnificent night flier in sporting contest

blocks.note: superb means magnificent
an owl hunts by night

explanation.surface: A splendid owl takes part in a competition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Super Bowl is the annual championship game of American professional football.

clue.text: Not a principal unfinished fraction

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is never reached and so is dropped

blocks.note: a third party is someone involved who is not one of the main parties to an agreement

explanation.surface: A minor share in a deal, still incomplete.
explanation.definitionFit: A third part is one of three equal portions of a whole, which is a fraction.

clue.text: Home provided for a pound for quiet creature about to be so!

indicators.note: about means going round, so the creature wraps around the call for silence

blocks.note: taken as written
L, from Latin libra, is the symbol for a pound
quiet as a mouse
sh is what you say to tell someone to be quiet

explanation.surface: A charity provides a pound to house a timid little animal, asking it to keep its voice down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so' points back to 'quiet', so 'to be so' means 'be quiet!', which is SH.
explanation.definitionFit: An almshouse is a charitable dwelling provided for poor or elderly people to live in.

clue.text: Sound of waterfall as a rule  ...

indicators.note: sound of means we want a word that is said the same as another

blocks.note: rain is literally water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: A waterfall makes a noise, as it always does; the dots run on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waterfall' is not a cascade but water falling as rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's sovereign authority over a kingdom, or the period it lasts, is what the noun means; the verb is the governing itself.

clue.text: Prince playing for Oxford or Cambridge?

definitions.text: Prince playing for Oxford or Cambridge?

blocks.clueFragment: Prince playing for Oxford or Cambridge?
blocks.note: surface reading: a young royal turning out for one of the two ancient universities
setter's reading: a sportsman picked for either university earns a Blue, and Oxford and Cambridge are also names of shades of that colour

explanation.surface: A prince representing his university in sport.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford and Cambridge a sportsman who represents the university against the other is called a Blue; a prince who did so would be a royal one.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal blue is a deep bright shade of the colour, sitting alongside Oxford blue and Cambridge blue.

clue.text: ...  from land and water in Africa

blocks.note: first meaning: a West African country
second meaning: the great West African river that gives the country its name

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, rain falls on the land and water of an African nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a landlocked republic of West Africa and to the major river flowing through it.

clue.text: Russian girl with some facial hair in North America

indicators.note: in means the facial hair is placed inside the abbreviation for the continent

blocks.note: a, meaning some or one
tash is British slang for a moustache
NA is the abbreviation for North America

explanation.surface: A Russian girl sporting a slight moustache is living in the USA or Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: Natasha is a common Russian female first name, a pet form of Natalya.

clue.text: Dives with French soldier and graduate among cats

indicators.note: among means in the midst of, so the soldier and graduate go inside the word for cats

blocks.note: Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts
mog is British slang for a cat

explanation.surface: Someone plunges in among cats with a French soldier and a graduate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dives' looks like a verb but is the rich man of the Bible parable of Dives and Lazarus.
explanation.definitionFit: Dives is the traditional name of the rich man in Luke's parable, and moneybags is slang for a wealthy person.

clue.text: See 5 across
Rubbish on the front page about Poles having to change vessels

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rubbish goes round the poles

blocks.note: trash is rubbish
N and S are the north and south poles
the front page is page i, the first roman numeral page, with P for page

explanation.surface: A newspaper splashes a rubbish story about Polish people having to switch ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' are not Polish people but the two compass poles; preliminary pages of a book are numbered in roman numerals, so i is the front page.
explanation.definitionFit: To transship is to transfer cargo or passengers from one ship or vehicle to another.

clue.text: Proceed with your remarks about a year, my boy

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the boy goes round the other letters

blocks.note: taken as written
Y is the abbreviation for year
a son is one's boy

explanation.surface: A parent invites their son to carry on speaking about a year of his life.
explanation.definitionFit: Say on is an old-fashioned imperative inviting a speaker to continue talking.

clue.text: Make an assumption from 4

indicators.note: from means made out of, so the new word is built from the letters of another

blocks.note: the answer to 4 down, its letters then rearranged

explanation.surface: Draw a conclusion based on another clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward a proposition as a basis for argument, to assume it as true.

clue.text: Fantastic Shakespearean copper in a painting the wrong way round

indicators.note: in places the metal inside the word for a painting
the wrong way round means read from right to left

blocks.note: an oil is a painting in oils
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A wonderful Shakespearean policeman appears upside down in a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: CU goes between OI and L, then the whole is read backwards. The cast list of Measure for Measure describes Lucio as 'a fantastic', meaning a fop.
explanation.definitionFit: In the play's list of characters, Lucio is labelled 'a fantastic', an old word for an extravagant, foppish man.

clue.text: Kind solver (who else?) with striking recommendation of DIY psychiatry

blocks.note: a sort is a kind
the solver of this clue is none other than you
workers on strike are out

explanation.surface: A kindly reader sets about solving with a dramatic piece of self-help advice.
explanation.walkthrough: '(who else?)' nudges the solver to see that the solver is the reader.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling someone to sort themselves out is advising them to fix their own mental or emotional problems unaided.

clue.text: An Italian writer in no hurry

blocks.note: taken as written
Dante Alighieri, author of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: An Italian author takes his time.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is the musical direction for a moderately slow, walking tempo, so it is unhurried.

clue.text: Journeyman taking tea instead of usual start to breakfast?

indicators.note: instead of usual start means the first letter is swapped out for a different one

blocks.note: tea is pronounced like the letter T
brekker is jokey British slang for breakfast

explanation.surface: A travelling worker drinks tea rather than eating his usual morning meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Journeyman' suggests a qualified tradesman, but here it is read literally as a man on a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A trekker is someone who makes a long, arduous journey on foot, literally a man on a journey.
